solution: The even natural numbers are \(2, 4, 6, 8, \ldots\) and they never end. In roster form: \(\{2, 4, 6, 8, \ldots\}\).
A prime number that is even must be divisible by 2, so the only even prime number is \(2\). Between 1 and 50 there is exactly one such number. In roster form: \(\{2\}\).
The negative integers are \(-1, -2, -3, \ldots\) and they continue without end. In roster form: \(\{-1, -2, -3, \ldots\}\).
The seven basic sounds (sur) of the sargam are Sa, Re, Ga, Ma, Pa, Dha, Ni. In roster form: \(\{\text{Sa, Re, Ga, Ma, Pa, Dha, Ni}\}\).

\(-2\) is not an element of set \(\mathbb{N}\) (the set of natural numbers).
\(P\) is the set of all \(p\) such that \(p\) is an odd number.

Listing method lists the actual elements; rule method states the common property. For example:

Set A (vowels of the English alphabet) — Listing: \(A = \{a, e, i, o, u\}\); Rule: \(A = \{x \mid x \text{ is a vowel of the English alphabet}\}\).

Set B (first five natural numbers) — Listing: \(B = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5\}\); Rule: \(B = \{x \mid x \in \mathbb{N},\ x \le 5\}\).
The Indian solar year has 12 months. By listing method: \(A = \{\text{Chaitra, Vaishakh, Jyeshth, Ashadh, Shravan, Bhadra, Ashwin, Kartik, Agrahayan, Paush, Magh, Phalgun}\}\).
The word 'COMPLEMENT' uses the letters C, O, M, P, L, E, N, T (repeated letters are written only once). By listing method: \(X = \{\text{C, O, M, P, L, E, N, T}\}\).
The five human sensory organs are the nose, ears, eyes, tongue and skin. By listing method: \(Y = \{\text{Nose, Ears, Eyes, Tongue, Skin}\}\).
The prime numbers from 1 to 20 are 2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17 and 19. By listing method: \(Z = \{2, 3, 5, 7, 11, 13, 17, 19\}\).
The world has seven continents. By listing method: \(E = \{\text{Asia, Africa, Europe, Australia, Antarctica, South America, North America}\}\).
Each element is a perfect square: \(1 = 1^2,\ 4 = 2^2,\ \ldots,\ 100 = 10^2\), i.e. \(n^2\) for \(n = 1\) to \(10\). By rule method: \(A = \{x \mid x = n^2,\ n \in \mathbb{N},\ n \le 10\}\).

Each element is a multiple of 6: \(6 = 6\times 1,\ 12 = 6\times 2,\ \ldots,\ 48 = 6\times 8\), i.e. \(6n\) for \(n = 1\) to \(8\). By rule method: \(B = \{x \mid x = 6n,\ n \in \mathbb{N},\ n < 9\}\).
The elements S, M, I, L, E are the letters of the word 'SMILE'. By rule method: \(C = \{x \mid x \text{ is a letter of the word 'SMILE'}\}\).
The elements are the seven days of a week. By rule method: \(D = \{x \mid x \text{ is a day of a week}\}\).
The elements a, e, t are the letters of the word 'eat'. By rule method: \(X = \{x \mid x \text{ is a letter of the word 'eat'}\}\).

Find each set. \(A = \{x \mid 3x - 1 = 2\}\): \(3x = 3\), so \(x = 1\), giving \(A = \{1\}\). \(B\) is the natural number that is neither prime nor composite, which is only \(1\), so \(B = \{1\}\). \(C = \{x \mid x \in \mathbb{N},\ x < 2\} = \{1\}\). All three sets have exactly the same element, so \(A = B = C\).
The only even prime number is \(2\), so \(A = \{2\}\). For \(B\): \(7x - 1 = 13\) gives \(7x = 14\), so \(x = 2\), giving \(B = \{2\}\). Both sets have the same element, so \(A = B\).
There is no natural number smaller than zero (natural numbers start at 1), so the set has no element. \(A = \varnothing\); it is an empty set.
\(x^2 = 0\) gives \(x = 0\), so \(B = \{0\}\). The set contains the element \(0\), so it is not an empty set.
\(5x - 2 = 0\) gives \(x = \frac{2}{5}\), which is not a natural number. So no natural number satisfies the condition. \(C = \varnothing\); it is an empty set.
\(A = \{x \mid x < 10,\ x \text{ is a natural number}\} = \{1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9\}\). The elements can be counted (9 of them), so \(A\) is a finite set.
\(B = \{y \mid y < -1,\ y \text{ is an integer}\} = \{-2, -3, -4, \ldots\}\). The elements never end, so \(B\) is an infinite set.
The number of Class 9 students in a school is fixed and can be counted, so \(C\) is a finite set.
The number of people in a village is fixed and can be counted, so this is a finite set.
The apparatus in a laboratory is limited in number and can be counted, so this is a finite set.
The whole numbers are \(0, 1, 2, 3, \ldots\) and they never end, so the set of whole numbers is an infinite set.
Between any two rational numbers there lies another rational number, so they cannot be counted; the set of rational numbers is an infinite set.
